newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African wool prices higher at latest auction.
newsitem.headline: S.African wool prices higher at latest auction.

text.p: South African wool prices were higher at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said.
It said 9,722 bales were offered at this week's sale, of which 96.8 percent was sold.

Price quotes for long Merino fleeces of 20 micron rose 3.0 percent, 21 micron rose 7.7 percent, 22 micron rose 8.8 percent, 23 micron rose 5.6 percent, 24 micron rose 4.0 percent and 25 micron rose 1.4 percent.
Prices for Merino bellies rose 2.9 percent, Merino lambs rose 5.2 percent and Merino locks rose 0.7 percent.
The offering included 1,807 bales of other White Wools, 1,456 bales of Ciskei/Transkei, 1,841 bales of Lesotho and 1,219 bales of coarse and coloured.

Of the 272 bales of 20 micron offered, 93.8 percent was sold. Of the 1,094 bales of 21 micron offered, 94.3 percent was sold. Of the 1,527 bales of 22 micron offered, 95.3 percent was sold. Of the 1.032 bales of 23 micron offered, 99.0 percent was sold and all bales of 24 and 25 micron offered, sold one hundred percent.
The next sale will take place on June 4, when about 10,000 bales will be on offer.
